system.description:
After you damage a creature with your Primary or Secondary Weapon, or successfully damage a creature with a Tech Domain card, you may apply one Intrusion.

Each creature may only have one Intrusion from you at a time. Applying another replaces the previous one.

Intrusion

Effect

Expose

The next attack against the target has Advantage. Then the Intrusion fades.

Jam

The target has Disadvantage on its next attack. Then the Intrusion fades.

Interference

Reduce the damage die of the target's next attack by one step. Then the Intrusion fades.

Trace

You always know the target's location until the end of the scene.

Spend 3 Hope to spread your intrusion. Choose one creature affected by one of your @UUID[Compendium.daggerheart-scifi-content.character-options.y4cUUgwOuWBlzF1e]{Intrusions}. Up to 3 adversaries within Very Close range of the target suffer the same Intrusion.
Hackers manipulate the battlefield through information warfare, cyber intrusion, and electronic disruption. They turn every piece of technology into a weapon.
You don't need to breathe and can survive the cold vacuum of space. You don't eat but must periodically recharge.
Once per Long Rest, reroll an Action Roll using Knowledge or Finesse.
You have advantage on rolls to negotiate with criminals, detect lies, or find a safe place to hide.

system.description: Whenever you spend Hope to use a Midnight Domain card, you are immediately Hidden.
The first weapon attack you make while Hidden gains an increased damage die (d6 -> d8, d8 -> d10, etc.).
Once per scene, immediately after damaging a creature, you may teleport into a shaded area within Far range.
Synthetic humanoids built with artificial bodies and genuine personalities. Androids are biomechanical constructs who typically resemble humanoids with glowing circuitry.

Spend a Hope to make a Spellcast Roll and conjure throwing blades that strike out at all targets within Very Close range. Targets you succeed against take d8+2 magic damage using your Proficiency.

If a target you hit is Vulnerable, they take an extra 1d8 damage.

system.description:
Being part of a slyborne community means you come from a group that operates outside the law, including all manner of criminals, grifters, and con artists. Being part of a slyborne community means you come from a group that operates outside the law, including all manner of criminals, grifters, and con artists. Members of slyborne communities are brought together by their disreputable goals and their clever means of achieving them. Many people in these communities have an array of unscrupulous skills: forging, thievery, smuggling, and violence. People of any social class can be slyborne, from those who have garnered vast wealth and influence to those without a coin to their name. To the outside eye, slyborne might appear to be ruffians with no loyalty, but these communities possess some of the strictest codes of honor which, when broken, can result in a terrifying end for the transgressor.

Slyborne are often calculating, clever, formidable, perceptive, shrewd, and tenacious.

Mark a Stress to boost the equipment of an ally within Close range or your own equipment. Apply one of these effects to your target:

  • Add 1d6 damage to the next successful attack made by the target with a primary weapon.

  • Grant +2 Evasion to the target until they are hit by an attack.
A direct neural implant allowing instant interaction with nearby technology.
